lesson_title: One Voice Against the Wind: Labour Rights and Collective Bargaining
hook_text: One worker asking is a request. Every worker asking is a negotiation.
clip_script: Picture one worker at the manager's door: 'The wage is too low.' The manager looks past him — at the queue outside the gate, a hundred people wanting his job. What weight does one voice carry? Almost none. Alone, a worker negotiates against the wind. Now picture ALL the workers at that door, together, one spokesperson: 'The wage is too low — for all of us.' Suddenly the manager isn't weighing one replaceable person against a queue. He's weighing the whole factory's output against the demand. THAT is the union: many weak voices, braided into one strong one — the stokvel principle, applied to work. And the law doesn't just allow it — the Constitution guarantees it: join, organise, bargain, and when all else fails, strike. Three rulebooks stand behind you: one for the arguing day, one floor under every ordinary day, one fund for the worst day. And when talks deadlock? A free referee's room, and a ladder: talk, guided talk, decision. The old war of the mill floor — converted into rules.
visual_style: A lone silhouette at a vast door blown by wind, then hundreds of silhouettes braiding into one glowing rope-figure; three rulebooks materialising on a shelf; a three-rung ladder rising in a referee's room.
pacing: Quiet lone-voice open, swelling to the braid, brisk institutional tour, resonant close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and know your rights before your first payslip.
